thread:
laura_sales: Customer (health POC) asks for a tiny handoff: preserve client IP for audit, allow TLS-inspect, SNI rewrite concerns, and an exact egress allowlist they can paste into firewall. Also want a 2-week cost note comparing PrivateLink vs peering.

tom_netops: Short recomendation: Peering = src-IP preserved end-to-end. PrivateLink = faster, but typically NATs to endpoint EIP unless you run a proxy/NLB. Dedicated supports proxy-protocol.

mina_infra: POC patterns: 1) PrivateLink + customer NLB + reverse-proxy -> X-Forwarded-For preserved. 2) Cross-account VPC peering -> native src-IP preserved.

security_ops: If their TLS inspector rewrites SNI or terminates mTLS, cert pinning/mTLS can break. Mitigation: terminate mTLS at their edge and use app-level auth, or request Dedicated with mutual TLS.

tom_netops: Pasteable allowlist (replace placeholders):
```
# OUTBOUND allowlist for Redwood POC
allow tcp from 10.0.0.0/16 to <REDWOOD_EIP_1> 443
allow tcp from 10.0.0.0/16 to <REDWOOD_EIP_2> 443
allow udp from 10.0.0.0/16 to <REDWOOD_EIP_1> 123
```

mina_infra: 2-week POC cost note: PrivateLink = small endpoint hourly + per-GB processing (~$0.02-0.05/hr + $0.01-0.05/GB); Peering = no endpoint-hour fee but possible AZ/region transfer costs. For ~100GB expect O($10-100) depending on region and topology.

laura_sales: Perfect, I'll send this with NetOps contact request and the SOC items. Thanks!
